# Environment variables

Every variable the binaries read. Env overrides the TOML base file at `$ESCUREL_CONFIG`.

## Server

escurel-server.

| var | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ESCUREL_CONFIG` | — | path to a TOML base file; env vars override it |
| `VERSION` | 0.0.0-dev | body of `GET /version` (alias of `ESCUREL_VERSION`) |
| `ESCUREL_VERSION` | 0.0.0-dev | body of `GET /version` |
| `ENV` | dev | log field `env` (alias of `ESCUREL_ENV`) |
| `ESCUREL_ENV` | dev | log field `env` |
| `ESCUREL_SERVER_DATA_DIR` | /data | host-volume root for DuckDB + FsStore + tenants |
| `ESCUREL_SEED_DIR` | — | markdown corpus seeded into the tenant at boot (idempotent), e.g. `examples/crm-demo` |
| `ESCUREL_WEBHOOK_URL` | — | outbound capture webhook; fire-and-forget POST of each new `capture_event` (M7) |
| `ESCUREL_SERVER_LISTEN_HTTP` | 0.0.0.0:8080 | HTTP listener (MCP/WS/REST) |
| `ESCUREL_TENANT` | default | single-tenant indexer's tenant id |
| `ESCUREL_REBUILD_INDEX_ON_BOOT` | if-missing | derived-index boot policy: `if-missing` (reuse an existing DuckDB; rebuild only when absent, and the default everywhere including the container) or `always` (drop + rebuild from the markdown LaneStore each start — re-embeds the whole corpus, so expect minutes) |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_BACKEND` | fs | `fs`, `s3`, `gcs` or `duckvfs` |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_DUCKVFS_ROOT` | — | root URL, e.g. `gdrive://escurel/lanes` or `sharepoint://escurel/lanes` (backend=duckvfs); its scheme picks the filesystem and the extension that is loaded |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_DUCKVFS_EXTENSION` | — | path to a built `gdrive.duckdb_extension` (backend=duckvfs); needed for every scheme, not only `gdrive://`. Prefer `…_EXTENSION_REPO` — a path is a local build a container does not have |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_DUCKVFS_EXTENSION_REPO` | — | `community` (the DuckDB community repository) or a repository URL, used when `…_EXTENSION` is unset. Setting NEITHER skips the load rather than failing, so the store opens and the first WRITE fails on a missing `write_blob` |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_DUCKVFS_DRIVE_ID` | — | Shared Drive id `0A…`; REQUIRED for a `gdrive://` root, else the store would silently target the credential's My Drive |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_DUCKVFS_DRIVE_SCOPE` | …/auth/drive | OAuth scope; the default is read/write because the extension's own `drive.readonly` default cannot serve a lane store |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_DUCKVFS_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` | 6 | tries per lane operation (the first counts) when the VFS answers a transient error (`temporary Drive API failure`, a rate limit, a 5xx, a timeout); `1` turns retrying off. Permanent errors (not found, permission, quota) are never retried |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_DUCKVFS_RETRY_MAX_BACKOFF_MS` | 30000 | longest wait between two tries; the wait starts at 500 ms, doubles, and is jittered into its upper half |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_DUCKVFS_RETRY_TOTAL_MS` | 180000 | once an operation has been failing this long its next transient error is returned instead of retried (a cold boot on a Drive lane touches hundreds of objects, so this bounds the stall of ONE object, not the boot) |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_DUCKVFS_SHAREPOINT_TENANT_ID` | — | Entra tenant id for a `sharepoint://` root (backend=duckvfs); REQUIRED for that scheme and refused for any other |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_DUCKVFS_SHAREPOINT_CLIENT_ID` | — | Entra app (client) id for a `sharepoint://` root; REQUIRED for that scheme |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_DUCKVFS_SHAREPOINT_CLIENT_SECRET` | — | the app's client secret for a `sharepoint://` root; never logged or printed. Prefer `…_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE` so the secret is mounted rather than exported. Exactly one of the two is REQUIRED |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_DUCKVFS_SHAREPOINT_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE` | — | path to a file holding the client secret (surrounding whitespace trimmed); the alternative to `…_CLIENT_SECRET`, refused when both are set |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_DUCKVFS_SHAREPOINT_DRIVE_ID` | — | Graph drive id `b!…` of the document library the paths hang off; exactly one of this and `…_SITE_ID` is REQUIRED, else the store would have no library to root the paths in |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_DUCKVFS_SHAREPOINT_SITE_ID` | — | Graph site id (`host,siteId,webId`), resolved to the site's default library; the alternative to `…_DRIVE_ID` |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_DUCKVFS_SHAREPOINT_GRAPH_SCOPE` | — | OAuth scope override (`GRAPH_SCOPE`); the extension defaults to `<graph endpoint>/.default` |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_GCS_BUCKET` | — | GCS bucket (backend=gcs) |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_GCS_PREFIX` |  | GCS key prefix (backend=gcs) |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_GCS_CREDENTIALS_PATH` | — | service-account key file (backend=gcs); unset = ADC, i.e. the metadata server on GCP |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_GCS_ENDPOINT` | — | GCS endpoint override (backend=gcs); emulator/tests only |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_S3_BUCKET` | — | S3 bucket (backend=s3) |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_S3_ENDPOINT` | — | S3 endpoint URL (backend=s3) |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_S3_PREFIX` |  | S3 key prefix (backend=s3) |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_S3_REGION` | us-east-1 | S3 region label (backend=s3) |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | — | S3 access key (backend=s3) |
| `ESCUREL_STORAGE_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | — | S3 secret key (backend=s3) |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_OIDC_ISSUER` | — | OIDC issuer; unset → unauthenticated dev mode |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_OIDC_AUDIENCE` | escurel | OIDC audience |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_TENANT_CLAIM` | tenant | JWT claim carrying the tenant id |
| `ESCUREL_WRITE_ACL` | enforce | per-instance write ACL: `enforce` (reject; the default, also for an unrecognised value) \| `log` (warn but allow) \| `off` (no check, explicit opt-out). Symmetric to the read ACL: owner-or-admin writes; public/no-owner instances are admin-write-only. |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_ADMIN_ROLE_CLAIM` | roles | JWT claim listing roles |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_ADMIN_ROLE_VALUE` | escurel:admin | role value granting admin |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_OPERATOR_ROLE_VALUE` | escurel:operator | role value (in the admin role claim) marking an OPERATOR credential, the only one that may name another tenant in the cross-tenant admin tools (tenant registry, tenant_export/tenant_import) |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_ROLE_TOOLS` | — | service roles and the only tools each may call, `role=tool,tool;role=tool` (e.g. `app:worker=list_events,expand,create_draft`); a token whose groups carry a listed role is refused every other tool and the `/ingest`, `/blob` and `/ws` surfaces. Agent-scope tools only; boot fails on an unknown tool |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_JWKS_REFRESH_SECS` | 300 | JWKS cache TTL (seconds) |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_JWKS_URI` | derived from issuer | explicit JWKS URL (e.g. Triton's `<issuer>/.well-known/jwks.json`) |
| `ESCUREL_RUN_PROGRESS_KEEP` | 50 | how many `run-progress` snapshots a run keeps (pruned at capture) |
| `ESCUREL_RUN_TRANSCRIPT_RETENTION_DAYS` | 90 | days a run transcript (`put_run_transcript`, read via `fetch_blob{run_id}`) is kept; swept every 30 s; `0` keeps them forever |
| `ESCUREL_EVENT_CLAIM_BOOT_GRACE_SECS` | 3600 | after a gateway start, how long `claim_event` withholds an event captured before the start that has no lease row (`claimed: false`, holder `(recovering)`), so a runner still running it under a lease the restart forgot can `renew_claim` it first. Events captured after the start are claimable at once. The default is the longest lease a claim may ask for; set it to your longest `ESCUREL_RUNNER_CLAIM_LEASE` to let an unheld backlog flow sooner, `0` turns it off |
| `ESCUREL_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECS` | 25 | how long a graceful stop waits for in-flight requests before aborting them (keep below the orchestrator's kill timeout) |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_SIGNING_KEY` | — | RSA private key (PKCS#8 or PKCS#1 PEM) the gateway signs `mint_agent_token` bearers with; unset → the tool refuses `unsupported` |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_SIGNING_KID` | derived | the `kid` those bearers carry (must be in a trusted JWKS) |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_SIGNING_ISSUER` | the OIDC issuer | the `iss` those bearers carry (must be a trusted issuer) |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_OIDC_ISSUER_2` | — | optional SECOND trusted issuer (e.g. Carl, for the dashboard's self-minted token); shares the audience + tenant claim |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_JWKS_URI_2` | derived from issuer #2 | explicit JWKS URL for the second issuer (e.g. Carl's `<issuer>/jwks.json`) |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_OIDC_ISSUER_<N>` | — | further trusted issuers, read as a contiguous `_2.._N` sequence (e.g. `_3` = the escurel-explore BFF's browser auth bridge); a gap stops the scan |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_JWKS_URI_<N>` | derived from issuer #N | explicit JWKS URL for the Nth issuer |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_BRIDGE_ISSUER` | — | the trusted issuer that is a chat bridge (`escurel-chat-bridge`); must be `ESCUREL_AUTH_OIDC_ISSUER` or an `ESCUREL_AUTH_OIDC_ISSUER_<N>` (boot fails otherwise, or when `ESCUREL_AUTH_BRIDGE_KID` is set without it). EVERY token verified against this entry is a bridge token, whatever kid it names: it lives at most 900 s, is never admin or operator, honours no roles or groups (group-granted ACLs do not apply to it), is refused if it carries an `agent`/`skill`/`run_id`/`purpose`/`act` claim, must name its channel in `bridge_channel`, and what it captures is stamped `captured_via: bridge:<channel>`. Serve its JWKS over https: whoever controls that response controls which keys sign as the bridge |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_BRIDGE_KID` | — | comma-separated key ids the bridge signs under; a pin on the `ESCUREL_AUTH_BRIDGE_ISSUER` entry: a token from it under any other kid is refused, and so is a token from another issuer under one of these kids. The key must be the bridge's own, never the gateway's main signing key. REQUIRED with `ESCUREL_AUTH_BRIDGE_ISSUER` |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_BRIDGE_TENANT` | — | the one tenant the bridge's tokens may name; REQUIRED with `ESCUREL_AUTH_BRIDGE_ISSUER` and must equal `ESCUREL_TENANT` (boot fails otherwise), so a gateway for another tenant cannot be configured to trust the same bridge. A bridge token naming another tenant is refused (`401`) |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_BRIDGE_CHAT_SKILL` | chat | the only `label_skill` a bridge token may `capture_event` under (= the bridge's `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_CHAT_SKILL`). A bridge token may call only `whoami`, `update_page` (create-if-absent of a `chat: {page_bound: true}` instance), `append_message` (`role: user`, page-bound groups), `list_messages` (page-bound groups), `capture_event` (this label) and `ingest_upload`; everything else is `-32003`, and `/ingest`, `/blob` and `/ws` answer `403` |
| `ESCUREL_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER` | gemini | `zero`, `gemini`, `alibaba`, `openai-compatible`, or `embeddinggemma` (a candle BERT-family sentence-transformer; ONLY in a binary built with `--features embeddinggemma`: the default build and the image refuse to boot with it). `gemini` with no key falls back to zero; `alibaba`/`openai-compatible` without a key file is a load failure. `hetzner` is refused: it serves no embeddings. Changing the provider or model re-embeds the corpus at the next boot |
| `ESCUREL_EMBEDDING_OPENAI_BASE_URL` | alibaba: https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 | `…/v1` base of the OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint (`alibaba`, `openai-compatible`); https, or plain http to loopback only |
| `ESCUREL_EMBEDDING_OPENAI_API_KEY_FILE` | — (required) | file holding the embeddings API key (a mounted secret); the key itself is never an env var |
| `ESCUREL_EMBEDDING_OPENAI_BATCH` | alibaba 10, else 16 | texts per `/embeddings` request |
| `ESCUREL_EMBEDDING_OPENAI_SEND_DIMENSIONS` | true | send `dimensions` (= `ESCUREL_EMBEDDING_DIM`); turn off for a model that rejects it — the returned length is checked either way |
| `ESCUREL_EMBEDDING_MODEL` | provider default | model id (alibaba default: `text-embedding-v4`; candle default: `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5`, a BERT sentence-transformer — the candle backend has no Gemma3 path yet, see #299) |
| `ESCUREL_EMBEDDING_DEVICE` | cpu | candle device (informational; CPU only today) |
| `ESCUREL_EMBEDDING_DIM` | 768 | vector dimension |
| `ESCUREL_EMBEDDER_REQUIRED` | false | when `true`, a failed real-embedder load aborts boot instead of silently degrading to zero-vector (FTS-only) retrieval (#299) |
| `ESCUREL_INDEX_BACKEND` | single-file | `single-file` or `ducklake` — selects the [`escurel_index::snapshot::IndexStore`] backend (DuckLake PR 6) |
| `ESCUREL_ROLE` | writer | `writer` or `reader` — `reader` requires `ESCUREL_INDEX_BACKEND=ducklake`; a reader boots with NO local single-file DuckDB, adopting the lake's newest published snapshot instead |
| `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_CATALOG_DSN` | — | DuckLake catalog DSN — a Postgres key/value DSN (contains `=`) or a DuckDB-file catalog path; required when `ESCUREL_INDEX_BACKEND=ducklake` |
| `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_DATA_PATH` | — | DuckLake `DATA_PATH` — `gs://…`, `s3://…`, `gdrive://…`, or a local directory; required when `ESCUREL_INDEX_BACKEND=ducklake` |
| `ESCUREL_CHAT_BACKEND` | postgres | `postgres` or `ducklake` — where chat history lives when `ESCUREL_INDEX_BACKEND=ducklake` and the catalog is Postgres |
| `ESCUREL_EVENTS_BACKEND` | postgres | as above, for the event bus |
| `ESCUREL_CRDT_PG_DSN` | the catalog DSN | Postgres holding `crdt_ops`/`crdt_snapshots`. Separate knob from the catalog because it holds customer document bytes, not lake metadata |
| `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_GCS_KEY_ID` | — | GCS HMAC key pair; required when `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_DATA_PATH` starts with `gs://` |
| `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_GCS_SECRET` | — | GCS HMAC key pair; required when `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_DATA_PATH` starts with `gs://` |
| `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_S3_ENDPOINT` | — | S3 (or MinIO) credentials; required when `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_DATA_PATH` starts with `s3://` |
| `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | — | S3 (or MinIO) credentials; required when `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_DATA_PATH` starts with `s3://` |
| `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | — | S3 (or MinIO) credentials; required when `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_DATA_PATH` starts with `s3://` |
| `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_S3_REGION` | us-east-1 | S3 (or MinIO) credentials; required when `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_DATA_PATH` starts with `s3://` |
| `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_S3_USE_SSL` | true | whether the S3/MinIO endpoint above is TLS |
| `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_GDRIVE_DRIVE_ID` | — | Shared Drive id `0A…`; required when `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_DATA_PATH` starts with `gdrive://`. Expect this to be SLOW — DuckLake writes many small files and Drive charges a round trip per file, with no atomic overwrite |
| `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_GDRIVE_SCOPE` | …/auth/drive | OAuth scope for the lake's Drive secret; credentials themselves come from ADC |
| `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_GDRIVE_EXTENSION` | — | path to a built `gdrive.duckdb_extension`; omit once it is installable by name from the community repository |
| `ESCUREL_DUCKLAKE_GDRIVE_PERMANENT_DELETE` | false | `true` makes the lake's retention GC delete expired Parquet on Drive for good (`gdrive_permanent_delete`) instead of moving it to the Drive trash, which is recoverable but counts against quota (~one object per capture/compaction). The lake data path is also declared `gdrive_immutable_prefixes` automatically: DuckLake never rewrites a data file in place |
| `ESCUREL_ALLOW_UNSIGNED_EXTENSIONS` | false | permit `LOAD` of a locally-built, unsigned DuckDB extension. Required for the `gdrive` paths above. Off by default: an unsigned extension is arbitrary native code in-process |
| `ESCUREL_SNAPSHOT_REFRESH_SECS` | 30 | a reader's background lake-poll interval (seconds); see `escurel_server::snapshot_refresh::RefreshTask` |
| `ESCUREL_SNAPSHOT_PUBLISH_SECS` | unset | a writer's optional periodic publish interval (seconds); an explicit `0` disables it (manual-only, via the `publish_snapshot` admin tool). Unset: disabled, UNLESS chat/events are lake-backed (`ESCUREL_CHAT_BACKEND` / `ESCUREL_EVENTS_BACKEND` = `ducklake`), where the task doubles as append-table compaction and unset defaults to `300` — see `resolve_publish_secs` / `escurel_server::snapshot_publish::PublishTask` |
| `ESCUREL_APPEND_COMPACT_MIN_FILES` | 8 | the publish task rewrites a lake-backed append table (events, drafts, chat) to one file only once it holds this many data files, so an idle tick uploads nothing and a read opens at most this many files; values below 2 mean "whenever a table has more than one file" (the old every-tick behaviour is `1`) |
| `ESCUREL_SNAPSHOT_KEEP` | 5 | how many DuckLake snapshots to retain after a successful publish; the GC pass never touches the current snapshot |
| `ESCUREL_WRITER_LEASE` | on | ducklake-writer single-writer boot guard (#371): a catalog advisory lock refused when another live writer holds it; `off` disables — only if you guarantee a single writer yourself |
| `ESCUREL_EGRESS_ALLOW_LOOPBACK` | false | outbound connector calls (REST/MCP rows, write-back) may reach `127.0.0.1`. `1`/`true`/`0`/`false` only. **Dev and tests only** — never in production (SSRF guard); any other value fails the boot |
| `ESCUREL_EGRESS_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` | 4194304 | cap on one upstream response (streamed; over the cap → the call fails). Whole number ≥ 1 |
| `ESCUREL_EGRESS_TIMEOUT_MS` | 10000 | total timeout of one upstream call; clamped to 30000. Whole number ≥ 1 |
| `ESCUREL_EGRESS_MAX_CONCURRENCY` | 8 | simultaneous upstream calls per endpoint. Whole number ≥ 1 |
| `ESCUREL_EGRESS_RATE_PER_SEC` | 50 | upstream calls per second per endpoint (token bucket). Whole number ≥ 1 |
| `ESCUREL_EGRESS_WRITE_RETRY_BACKOFF_MS` | 500 | base backoff between write-back retries (a test knob; leave unset in production). Whole number ≥ 0 |
| `ESCUREL_SECRET_<TENANT>__<NAME>` | — | a TENANT's credential, referenced as `secret_ref: gsm:<name>` or `env:ESCUREL_SECRET_<TENANT>__<NAME>` (injected from GCP Secret Manager). `<TENANT>` is the tenant id upper-cased, non-alphanumerics as `_` (`stuttgart-ai` → `STUTTGART_AI`); `<NAME>` holds no `__`, an id whose token holds `__` (`a--b`) has no env namespace, and two tenants may not share a token (`a-b` / `a_b`: refused at tenant creation). The namespace used to be global (`ESCUREL_SECRET_<NAME>`), so one tenant's admin could name another's secret |
| `ESCUREL_SECRET_ENV_ALLOW` | — | extra env var names a tenant may name as `env:NAME`: `tenant:NAME` for one tenant, a bare `NAME` for EVERY tenant (an explicit operator choice) |
| `ESCUREL_SECRET_FILE_DIRS` | /run/secrets | directories whose `<dir>/<tenant>/` sub-directory a tenant may name as `file:/path` (a tenant cannot read `<dir>/<other-tenant>/…`) |
| `ESCUREL_SQL_FILE_DIRS` | — | directories a `sqlite` credential's database file, and every `json_dir` / `parquet_dir` source's files, may live under (canonicalised; `..`, a symlink out and a glob reaching outside are refused). Unset refuses file databases AND directory sources. Postgres/MySQL credentials are checked like an endpoint: the connection string is parsed with libpq's grammar, only `host`, `hostaddr`, `port`, `dbname`, `user`, `password`, `sslmode`, `options`, `application_name`, `connect_timeout` are accepted (`service=`, `passfile=`, `sslrootcert=` … are refused), EVERY host/`hostaddr` must resolve to public addresses (loopback only with `ESCUREL_EGRESS_ALLOW_LOOPBACK`), and a host named by NAME is pinned to the address that was checked |
| `ESCUREL_SQL_OBJECT_PREFIXES` | — | comma-separated s3:// or gs:// bucket/directory prefixes allowed for json_dir and parquet_dir sources. A trailing slash is added to each prefix, so s3://bucket/demo permits only keys beneath demo/. Unset refuses remote directory sources. The setting authorises paths; DuckDB httpfs still needs its own credentials and endpoint (a DuckLake S3/GCS secret on the same connection, or DuckDB credential-chain configuration) |
| `ESCUREL_CURSOR_KEY` | random per process | signing key of the list cursors (`next_cursor`), at least 32 bytes (`openssl rand -hex 32`); a shorter one stops the server at boot. A cursor the server did not issue (forged, edited, issued before a restart) or issued for another tenant, skill or list answers `invalid_cursor`. Set the SAME value on every replica (writer + readers) of one deployment so a client may page across them |
| `ESCUREL_ROWS_QUERY_TIMEOUT_SECS` | 30 | how long one `instances: rows` source query may run before it is interrupted (and, for Postgres, cancelled by the server itself). Whole number of seconds ≥ 1 |
| `ESCUREL_SQL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECS` | 5 | libpq `connect_timeout` for a network database source (Postgres), so a black-holed host cannot hold the tenant's index connection for the OS TCP timeout. Whole number of seconds ≥ 1 |
| `ESCUREL_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS` | see `escurel_index::DEFAULT_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS` | per-query wall-clock bound on retrieval queries (#455); `0` disables the bound |
| `ESCUREL_MCP_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | 16777216 (16 MiB) | request-body limit of `POST /mcp` in bytes; a larger body is refused with 413 |
| `ESCUREL_INGEST_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | 16777216 (16 MiB) | request-body limit of `POST /ingest/upload` in bytes; the body is base64 JSON, so the file limit is about three quarters of it. The per-tenant `max_blob_bytes` quota still applies after decoding |
| `ESCUREL_EVENT_ACL` | off | per-event ACL on the event bus: `off` \\| `log` \\| `enforce` |
| `ESCUREL_TOOLCALL_DETAIL` | summary | what a run's recorded tool calls keep beyond sizes: `summary` (a bounded, redacted summary of each call's arguments and result, readable only by whoever may read the run) \\| `off` (sizes and timing only). An unrecognised value means `off` |
| `ESCUREL_AUTONOMY_LINT` | off | write-time lint of a skill page's `autonomy:` value: `off` \\| `log` \\| `enforce` |
| `ESCUREL_EMIT_EDIT_EVENTS` | false | `1`/`true`: emit an event per page edit (the eager per-edit improvement loop, #246) |
| `ESCUREL_INGEST_CONTEXTUALIZE` | structural | contextual-retrieval mode of ingested document chunks: `structural` or `off`; `llm` situates chunks with the endpoint below |
| `ESCUREL_CONTEXTUALIZE_LLM_ENDPOINT` | — | chat-completions endpoint used when `ESCUREL_INGEST_CONTEXTUALIZE=llm` |
| `ESCUREL_CONTEXTUALIZE_LLM_API_KEY` | — | bearer key for that endpoint |
| `ESCUREL_RETRIEVAL_RERANK` | `bge` when built with the `rerank` feature, else `off` | second-stage cross-encoder: `off` or `bge` |
| `ESCUREL_RETRIEVAL_RERANK_CANDIDATES` | 100 | how many first-stage candidates the reranker scores |
| `ESCUREL_RETRIEVAL_RERANK_MODEL` | BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 | reranker model id |
| `ESCUREL_RETRIEVAL_RERANK_DEVICE` | cpu | reranker device |
| `ESCUREL_RETRIEVAL_TWO_PASS` | false | Matryoshka two-pass vector search (`true`/`1`/`yes`/`on`) |
| `ESCUREL_RETRIEVAL_COARSE_DIM` | 128 | Matryoshka prefix length of the coarse pass (e.g. 128/256/512) |
| `ESCUREL_RETRIEVAL_COARSE_CANDIDATES` | 500 | candidates the coarse pass hands to the fine pass |
| `ESCUREL_OBSERVABILITY_METRICS_LISTEN` | 0.0.0.0:9090 | dedicated Prometheus `/metrics` listener; an explicitly empty value disables it |
| `ESCUREL_OBSERVABILITY_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | — | OTLP endpoint for traces (falls back to `ESCUREL_OTLP_ENDPOINT`); unset = no export |
| `ESCUREL_PACK_SECRET` | — | HMAC secret that signs/verifies skill packs (also read by `escurel admin pack …`) |
| `ESCUREL_OPERATION_SLUG_SECRET` | — | secret the async-operation slugs are derived with |
| `ESCUREL_SEARCH_MIN_SIMILARITY` | none (no floor) | minimum cosine similarity a vector candidate must clear to enter the vector arm; BM25 matches are never affected |
| `ESCUREL_SERVE_DEMO_DIR` | — | serve this directory (a built `escurel-explore` web bundle) at `/` |
| `ESCUREL_AUTH_GROUPS_CLAIM` | `roles` | JWT claim listing the caller's groups |
| `ESCUREL_INDEX_HNSW` | false | build the `vss` HNSW indexes (`true`/`1`/`yes`/`on`); off by default (large, slow to rebuild) |
| `ESCUREL_INDEX_EXTENSIONS` | — | comma-separated absolute paths of pre-built `.duckdb_extension` files to `LOAD` (the image bakes them) |

## Server / Runner

read by both the server and the runner.

| var | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ESCUREL_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | — | shared secret; when set the webhook body is HMAC-SHA256-signed via `X-Escurel-Webhook-Signature: sha256=<hex>` The runner requires the same HMAC signature on inbound `POST /trigger`. |
| `ESCUREL_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | — | OTLP endpoint (server: fallback of the variable above; runner: its only knob) |

## Server / Runner / Loader

read by several binaries.

| var | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ESCUREL_GEMINI_API_KEY` | — | Gemini API key (provider=gemini; unset → zero fallback) |

## Runner

escurel-runner (the agent runner). For an Evolve/Workbench deployment, probe
`GET /readyz` and admit planning work only after it returns 200. It becomes
ready after a successful write of its reserved `escurel:runner-status` record
(`report_runner_status`; an older gateway: a system event)
and becomes unready when that write is refused, fails, goes stale, or the
runner starts draining. Give the runner service credential `escurel:admin`
scope; keep per-run harness credentials caller-scoped. `GET /healthz` remains
a dependency-free liveness probe. Webhook-only runners without a configured
tenant/token can process `/trigger` but deliberately report unready at
`/readyz`, so do not use that probe as their traffic gate.

| var | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_LISTEN` | 0.0.0.0:8088 | address of the runner's own HTTP server (`/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/version`, `POST /trigger`) |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_GATEWAY_URL` | http://127.0.0.1:8080 | base URL of the escurel gateway exposing `/mcp` |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_ENV` | dev | deployment environment stamped on every log record |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_TENANT` | — | tenant whose inbox the poller drains; the poller is off when this or the token is absent |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_TOKEN` | — | tenant-scoped bearer the runner presents to `/mcp`; a static token wins over minting. A runner on a static token cannot mint, so every run of a skill with an `agent:` profile fails (dead-letters) there: agent profiles need a minting runner (`ESCUREL_RUNNER_AUTH_SIGNING_KEY`) |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_TOKEN_FILE` | — | a file holding the runner's bearer, kept fresh by a sidecar (a laptop or on-prem runner on a short-lived service credential); used when `ESCUREL_RUNNER_TOKEN` is unset, read at startup (an unreadable or empty file refuses to start) and re-read whenever it changes, so a rotated credential is used on the next gateway call (a runner whose calls came back `401` recovers without a restart). Like a static token it cannot mint |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_QUEUE_CAP` | 1024 | bound of the dispatch queue (backpressure instead of unbounded growth) |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_SEEN_CAP` | 4096 | bound of the dedup seen-set |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_POLL_INTERVAL` | 30s | interval between inbox polls (`30s`, `1500ms`, `2m`) |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_TAIL_MAX_AGE` | 10m | how old a request on a tailed label may be and still be acted on after a restart |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_STATUS_INTERVAL` | 5m | how often the runner refreshes its status record (`runner-status:<runner_id>`) when nothing changed; it travels in the record as `status_interval_s` |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_LABELS` | (none) | comma-separated labels this runner carries (`site:muc,has:sap-gui`); work whose `requires: {labels}` it lacks is left in the inbox for a runner that has them, and the labels are advertised on its `runtime` page. A labelled runner is a fleet member: its credential needs `escurel:admin` to claim (an error is logged at boot otherwise, and it takes no inbox work), and a webhook trigger it cannot route or claim at once is left to the poller |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_EXCLUSIVE` | false | take only inbox work whose SKILL page's `requires:` names one of this runner's labels or a harness it offers besides its default; recommended for laptop and on-prem runners, so they do not race the central runner for the whole inbox and an event's `provenance.requires` cannot steer arbitrary work onto them |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_PROBE_INTERVAL` | 10m | how often the runner re-probes its harness CLIs (`<cli> --version`) and rewrites its `runtime` page when a version or availability changed, without a restart. A CLI whose probe fails is `available: false` and gets no work that `requires:` its harness |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_CLAIM_LEASE` | max(60s, 4 x poll interval), capped at 60m | how long a `claim_event` lease on an inbox event lasts: 1s to 60m (the gateway's bound) and at least two poll intervals, or the runner refuses to start naming this key. A renewal task renews held leases every third of the lease, independent of the inbox poll; a dead runner's events become claimable this long after it stopped |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_HARNESS_ALLOW` | the configured harness | comma-separated harnesses a manual start may ask for by name; others fail closed |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_MODEL_ALLOW` | — | comma-separated models a skill page's `model:` may pick instead of the runner's configured one; others fail the run closed |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_CHAT_MODEL` | — | the model chat runs use instead of the runner's configured one, unless the skill page names its own `model:` |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_ID` | <HOSTNAME>:<pid> | this runner's name in its status reports |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_CANCEL_GRACE` | 5s | time a cancelled run's subprocess gets between SIGTERM and SIGKILL |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_LINT_INTERVAL` | disabled | how often the runner fires the `lint` skill (the scheduled semantic-health pass); a synthetic entry in the schedule loop, kept for compatibility |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_SCHEDULE_TICK` | 30s | how often the runner looks for skills whose `schedule:` window has opened (the worst-case lateness of a scheduled trigger; zero is refused) |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_SCHEDULE_GRACE` | 15m | how long after it opens a `schedule:` window may still fire (catch-up after a restart); an older window is not run late. Zero is refused; below the tick it is raised to the tick |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_LEDGER_PATH` | ./escurel-runner-ledger.duckdb | runner-local durable run ledger (its own DuckDB file; use a path under `/data` in a deployment) |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_HARNESS` | echo | harness adapter: `echo`, `claude`, `codex`, `agy`, `muse`, `gemini`, `gemini-vertex`, `alibaba`, `hetzner`, `openai-compatible`, `delegate` |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_CLAUDE_BIN` | claude | path to the `claude` binary |

| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_CODEX_BIN` | codex | path to the `codex` binary |

| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_AGY_BIN` | agy | path to the `agy` (Antigravity) binary |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_AGY_MODEL` | — | `--model` passed to `agy` |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_AGY_HOME` | the process HOME | home directory holding `agy`'s credentials |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_MUSE_BIN` | muse | path to the `muse` binary |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_MUSE_MODEL` | — | `--model` passed to `muse exec` |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_MUSE_CONFIG_HOME` | $XDG_CONFIG_HOME or $HOME/.config | config directory holding `muse`'s provider credentials |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_AUTH_ISSUER` | — | issuer of the bearers the runner MINTS for itself instead of holding a static token |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_AUTH_AUDIENCE` | escurel | audience of minted bearers |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_AUTH_KID` | derived from the key | `kid` of minted bearers |

## Bridge

escurel-chat-bridge (the Teams chat bridge, `docs/deploy/chat-bridge.md`).
It runs only when started; nothing else reads these.

| var | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_LISTEN` | 0.0.0.0:3978 | HTTP listener of `escurel-chat-bridge`: the platform's messaging endpoint `POST /api/messages`, plus `/healthz` and `/version` |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_STATE_PATH` | /data/escurel-chat-bridge.duckdb | the bridge's DuckDB state file: one row per platform message (the dedup key) and whether its one reply was sent. Durable state, not a cache: losing it lets a redelivered message be answered again |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_GATEWAY_URL` | — | REQUIRED: the gateway base URL the bridge calls `/mcp` on |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_TENANT` | — | REQUIRED: the tenant the bridge's tokens name |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_AUTH_ISSUER` | — | REQUIRED: the issuer the bridge signs the asker's short-lived token as; the gateway must trust it (primary or `ESCUREL_AUTH_OIDC_ISSUER_<N>`), name it in `ESCUREL_AUTH_BRIDGE_ISSUER`, and its JWKS must publish the bridge's own key |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_AUTH_AUDIENCE` | escurel | audience of the tokens the bridge signs |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_AUTH_KID` | — | REQUIRED: `kid` of the bridge's own signing key as the issuer's JWKS publishes it; the gateway must name the bridge's issuer in `ESCUREL_AUTH_BRIDGE_ISSUER` (which restricts every token from it) and list this kid in `ESCUREL_AUTH_BRIDGE_KID` |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_AUTH_SIGNING_KEY` | — | the bridge's OWN RSA private key (PEM, PKCS#1 or PKCS#8); never the gateway's or a runner's signing key, which would let a compromised bridge sign unrestricted tokens. Never logged. Exactly one of this and `…_FILE` is REQUIRED |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_AUTH_SIGNING_KEY_FILE` | — | path to a file holding the signing key; the alternative to `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_AUTH_SIGNING_KEY` |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_TEAMS_APP_ID` | — | REQUIRED: the bot's Microsoft app (client) id; the `aud` an inbound Bot Framework token must carry and the client id of the connector token |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_TEAMS_ALLOWED_TENANTS` | — | REQUIRED: comma-separated Entra tenant ids whose people the bridge answers; an activity whose `conversation.tenantId` / `channelData.tenant.id` is not listed is ignored |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_TEAMS_APP_PASSWORD` | — | the bot app's client secret, for the client-credentials connector token; never logged. Exactly one of this and `…_FILE` is REQUIRED |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_TEAMS_APP_PASSWORD_FILE` | — | path to a file holding the client secret; the alternative to `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_TEAMS_APP_PASSWORD` |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_TEAMS_OPENID_METADATA_URL` | https://login.botframework.com/v1/.well-known/openidconfiguration | OpenID metadata whose `jwks_uri` holds the keys inbound channel tokens are verified against |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_TEAMS_ISSUER` | https://api.botframework.com | the `iss` an inbound channel token must carry |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_TEAMS_TOKEN_URL` | https://login.microsoftonline.com/botframework.com/oauth2/v2.0/token | client-credentials token endpoint for replies; a single-tenant bot uses `https://login.microsoftonline.com/<entra tenant id>/oauth2/v2.0/token` |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_TEAMS_TOKEN_SCOPE` | https://api.botframework.com/.default | scope of the connector token |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_PRINCIPAL_TEMPLATE` | — | REQUIRED: the escurel subject for a Teams user: `{aadObjectId}` (Entra object id), `{userId}` (Teams user id) and `{tenantId}` (Entra tenant) are filled in, e.g. `user:{aadObjectId}`. The bridge refuses to start on an unknown placeholder or a template naming neither `{aadObjectId}` nor `{userId}` (it would map every sender to one subject). It must equal the `sub` the person's own token from the gateway's primary issuer carries, or their chats and the pages they may read will not line up. A message from a user lacking a named field is not answered |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_CHAT_SKILL` | chat | `label_skill` of the captured chat event (the runner answers it in chat mode); the gateway's `ESCUREL_AUTH_BRIDGE_CHAT_SKILL` must name the same skill |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_CONVERSATION_SKILL` | conversation | the page-bound conversation skill each person's Teams chat becomes an instance of (`chat: {page_bound: true}`, owner-private; the shipped chat corpus has one) |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_POLL_INTERVAL` | 1s | how often the bridge checks the chat group for the run's answer |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_TYPING_INTERVAL` | 3s | how often it re-sends the typing indicator while the run is live (Teams shows one for about three seconds) |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_REPLY_TIMEOUT` | 10m | how long it waits for an answer before telling the person it has none |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES` | 10485760 | largest attachment it downloads and uploads through `ingest_upload`; a larger one is listed in the message as not ingested |
| `ESCUREL_BRIDGE_TEAMS_ATTACHMENT_HOSTS` | *.sharepoint.com,*.asm.skype.com | comma-separated hosts (`*.suffix` = any subdomain) an attachment may be downloaded from besides the connector's own `serviceUrl` origin. Such a download must be https, resolve only to public addresses (loopback, private, link-local and CGNAT are refused after DNS resolution) and is not redirected; the bot's bearer goes only to the connector origin |

| `ESCUREL_ECHO_USAGE` | — | echo harness: report this usage (tests) |
| `ESCUREL_TEST_GDRIVE_EXTENSION` | — | path of a built gdrive extension for the duckvfs tests |
| `ESCUREL_TEST_MIGRATE_KIND_PAGE_DELAY_MS` | — | sleep this long before each page of `migrate_kind`, to give a CI-sized tenant a long migration window |
| `ESCUREL_SIGKILL_FULL` | — | `1`: run all ten kill points of the migrate-kind SIGKILL test (default: four) |
| `ESCUREL_SECRET_ACME__SURELY_UNSET_X` | — | a name the secret-policy tests assert is NOT set |
| `ESCUREL_RUNNER_BIN` | — | `escurel-test-support`'s `RunnerProcess`: the `escurel-runner` binary to start; unset uses the one next to the test executable (`target/<profile>/`) |
